models.collectorNote: With so few built, history is documented car by car; alloy-bodied Ghia cars sit at the top of a very small market.

generations.name: Vallelunga
generations.note: The Kent four was tuned to 104 hp; early cars carried alloy Ghia bodies, later ones glassfibre by Fissore.

models.intro: Alejandro de Tomaso's first road car: a mid-engined coupé with a backbone chassis, Ford Cortina power and Ghia or Fissore bodywork. Only about 58 were built, but the layout — mid-engine, Italian body, Ford engine — became the De Tomaso formula for thirty years.
models.name: Vallelunga

models.collectorNote: The spine chassis flexes and the cooling is marginal — sorted cars have documented fixes for both. Originality of the gullwing deck hardware matters.

generations.name: Mangusta
generations.note: European cars used the 289 (306 hp in Hi-Po tune); US cars took the 302 at 230 hp. The chassis was a development of the Vallelunga's spine.

models.intro: The mongoose — the animal that kills cobras — drawn by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Ghia around a backbone chassis and a Ford V8. Gullwing covers over the engine, a split rear deck, and proportions that still stop traffic. About 400 were built.
models.name: Mangusta

models.collectorNote: Dealer-sold volume means supply is real; the market splits on originality versus the (very common) modifications. ZF transaxle condition is the expensive question.

generations.name: Pantera / L / GTS / Group 4
generations.note: US-market cars were rated lower under SAE net figures as the seventies wore on; the Group 4 competition cars were the extreme of the line.

generations.name: Pantera GT5 / GT5-S / Si
generations.note: The GT5's wings and arches defined the eighties car; the 1990 Si restyle by Marcello Gandini brought the fuel-injected 5.0 and a new chassis under the familiar shape.

models.intro: The De Tomaso that conquered America: Tom Tjaarda's wedge, a Ford 351 Cleveland amidships, sold through Lincoln-Mercury dealers with a Ford warranty. Group 4 racers, the wide-body GT5 cars of the eighties, and the final Si — the Pantera outlived its maker-era rivals by two decades.
models.name: Pantera

models.collectorNote: Scarcity cuts both ways: values trail the Pantera's while parts shared with it are a blessing. Rust in the sills and floor is the known enemy.

generations.name: Longchamp / GTS
generations.note: Automatic gearboxes dominate; the rare manual GTS cars are the driver's pick. Figures quoted are the gross ratings of the period.

models.intro: De Tomaso's front-engined luxury coupé — Tjaarda again, Ford Cleveland power, and a chassis shared with the Deauville saloon and the Maserati Kyalami. About 409 coupés were built across a long, quiet production life, plus a handful of Spyder convertibles.
models.name: Longchamp

models.collectorNote: Production records are fragmentary — buy the car and its paperwork together, and expect to be the marque's archive for your own example.

generations.name: Guarà
generations.note: BMW-powered cars made 320 hp; the Ford-engined cars that followed were quoted up to 375. Coupé, Barchetta and Spider bodies were offered.

models.intro: The last De Tomaso: a carbon-kevlar and aluminium sports car with pushrod suspension, launched with BMW V8 power and finished, after Alejandro de Tomaso's stroke, in tiny numbers with Ford V8s. Fewer than 50 cars were completed.
models.name: Guarà
